thread_analysis.thread_summary: A large operational thread (26,648 lines, 7 messages) for the Alps Alpine (ALAP) UXC module Bluetooth + Wi-Fi Alliance certification project. The Bluetooth portion covers: Classic RF test (completed Oct 10, 2025), RF PHY test (BR/EDR and BLE, following RF test), and IOPT profile testing (MAP, PBAP, SPP). Key issues: (1) Customer's connection diagram for RF PHY test was missing the mandatory USB Serial DTM control path. (2) BLE RF PHY test requires QUTS Status App (not QRCT) to enter BLE DTM mode — customer's lab had neither and QRCT cannot substitute; QUTS is bundled with QRCT installer. (3) IOPT SPP test failed at lab; customer had a passing PTS report; solution proposed: use customer's PTS log as evidence. (4) IOPT adb connectivity issue: BlueSPP.apk install required Developer Mode + specific USB cable (DUT USB function cable, not debug cables). The thread also contains a Wi-Fi Alliance certification planning sub-thread (for the same UXC module) which is unrelated to Bluetooth SIG qualification.
all_questions_found: What is the correct connection diagram for Bluetooth RF PHY DTM testing (USB Serial control path missing)?
Can QRCT be used instead of QUTS Status App to enter BLE DTM mode on Qualcomm chipsets?
SPP IOPT test is failing at the lab but customer has a passing PTS report — can the customer's log be used as evidence?
What USB cable and settings are needed to install BlueSPP.apk via ADB for IOPT test setup?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: RF PHY (DTM) testing requires three connections: RF cable (DUT↔RF test system), USB Serial (DUT↔PC running QDART), and RS232/GPIB (PC↔RF test system). The customer's diagram lacked the USB Serial path. For BLE DTM on Qualcomm, QUTS Status App (at C:\Program Files (x86)\Qualcomm\QUTSStatusApp\QUTSStatusApp.exe) is the correct tool — QRCT handles Classic BT calibration and cannot control BLE DTM state. IOPT adb setup needs Developer Mode enabled and the correct USB cable (DUT USB function port, not the debug/JTAG cables). SPP failure resolution: use customer's passing PTS log as test evidence when lab environment cannot reproduce the pass.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: DTM test setup is fundamentally different from open-loop regulatory RF tests — always verify the serial control connection path in customer diagrams. QUTS and QRCT are separate Qualcomm tools with separate functions; they are distributed together but not interchangeable. Accepting customer PTS logs as evidence is an acceptable fallback when environment-related failures cannot be resolved.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Missing USB Serial control path → cannot enter DTM → RF PHY test blocked entirely. Using QRCT for BLE DTM → DTM mode cannot be entered → BLE test blocked. Endless retries of SPP failure without proposing customer log acceptance → wasted time and project delays.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: The initial miscommunication about QRCT substituting for QUTS (passed from Alps Alpine engineering) was accepted by the lab without verification, causing additional delay. The correct answer should have been checked with Allion's own RF test experts before attempting QRCT.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: For Qualcomm-chipset Bluetooth modules, prepare a QUTS Status App checklist at project kickoff. Always verify the customer's test setup diagram against the DTM test requirements before the DUT arrives at the lab — do not wait until testing is underway to find missing connections.
